Key_Finding: Concurrent flame spread accelerates sharply at 30% O2 under low forced ventilation (5-15 cm/s). Exhibits U-shaped flammability boundary with lower oxygen limit in 0g than 1g.
At ISS baseline (21% O2, 14.7 psi), flame spread is strictly oxygen-transport limited and scales linearly with low cabin ventilation flow velocity.
PMMA rods sustain burning at lower O2 concentrations in microgravity low-speed flows than in 1g upward testing; bursting vapor bubbles eject burning droplets.
At lunar habitat atmosphere (30% O2, 10.2 psi), thick acrylic burns over 2.4x faster than at 21% O2 and requires extended cooling to prevent re-ignition from hot melt.
High-performance aerospace polymers that self-extinguish at 21% O2 can propagate opposed and concurrent flames when oxygen reaches 30% O2.
Largest intentional spacecraft fire test at 21% O2; demonstrated that cabin-scale flames reach a steady limiting length governed by oxygen supply and duct confinement.
Validated NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 material screening limits in real 0g vehicle conditions; thin silicone sheets produce dense silica soot requiring post-fire HEPA filtration.
Higher ventilation flow (30 cm/s vs 20 cm/s) increased flame spread rate by ~31%, confirming ventilation control is the fastest first-line suppression mechanism.
Tested full-scale fire in lunar exploration atmosphere (30% O2, 10.2 psi); demonstrated rapid CO/CO2 spike and tested autonomous smoke/gas monitoring systems.
At 34% O2 and 8.2 psi exploration atmosphere, flame intensity and spread rate surge dramatically despite lower total pressure; oxygen mole fraction dominates fire risk.

Recommended_Suppression: Power Bus Isolation + Dual Sensor Alarm
Key_Finding: In microgravity, absence of buoyant plumes causes smoke particles to residence longer in hot zones and agglomerate into larger particles, delaying standard ionization detectors.
Smoldering cellulose behind equipment panels generates sub-micron and large agglomerated aerosols; combining optical scattering with CO gas sensing cuts detection lag by >50%.
Hot spherical droplet flames radiative-quench into invisible 'cool flames' (500-800 K) that continue producing toxic CO and formaldehyde and can unexpectedly re-ignite.

Recommended_Suppression: IR/UV Flame Sensing + Inert Gas Dilution
Key_Finding: Alcohol fuels burn with nearly invisible blue, soot-free spherical flames in microgravity, evading particulate smoke detectors and requiring UV/IR or CO/CO2 gas sensors.

Recommended_Suppression: Fuel Valve Cutoff + Inert Gas Purge
Key_Finding: Demonstrated gaseous cool flames and soot thresholds up to 85% O2; high oxygen dramatically increases radiative heat loss and soot shell formation.
Electric fields drive ion-driven convection that mimics partial-gravity buoyancy (0.16g-0.38g), reducing soot production and destabilizing flames near extinction.
Simulates burning solid regression using gaseous fuel stagnation flow; flames stay lit at ultra-low heat release rates in 0g where 1g flames blow off.
Measured soot volume fraction and temperature distributions in laminar microgravity flames, providing calibration baselines for optical flame detectors.
Materials self-extinguishing at 21% O2 (1g) can sustain flame propagation at 30% O2 when assisted by ventilation flows in reduced gravity.

Key_Finding: At 100% O2 (4.3 psi spacesuit atmosphere), ignition energy drops by an order of magnitude and flame spread accelerates rapidly; strict exclusion of ignition sources is mandatory.
